info.title: Rebase Grid API
info.description:
REST API for accessing power system data from TSOs worldwide.

## Multi-Source Architecture

Each area can have **multiple data sources** (e.g., ENTSO-E, Energy-Charts).
All data endpoints accept an optional `source` query parameter to select which source to query.
If omitted, the area's preferred source is used (configured per data type).

Use `GET /v1/areas` to discover available countries, bidding zones, control
areas, synchronous areas, and source coverage. Legacy `/v1/zone/*` metadata
paths remain available for existing clients.

## Data Types

| Type | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Production** | MW | Generation breakdown by production type |
| **Statistics** | varies | Period aggregate/reference datasets such as installed generation capacity |
| **Consumption** | MW | Total system load |
| **Price** | EUR/MWh | Day-ahead spot market price |
| **Exchange** | MW | Cross-border physical flows |
| **Frequency** | Hz | Grid frequency (per-second or per-minute) |

## Geopolygons

Versioned country borders, ENTSO-E bidding zones, ENTSO-E control areas, and a
license-clean electricitymaps zone layer are served under `/v1/geo` as raw
GeoJSON (`Content-Type: application/geo+json`), ready to drop straight into
geopandas, folium, leaflet, and QGIS without unwrapping. Each dataset is
versioned by ISO date and content hash (SHA256); request `?version=YYYY-MM-DD`
to pin, or omit for `latest`. Filter features with `?country=` (matches
`properties.countryKey`) or `?ids=` (comma-separated, matched against the
dataset's `feature_id_field`).

Use `GET /v1/geo` to list registered datasets — currently `world_zones`,
`entsoe_cty`, `entsoe_bzn`, and `entsoe_cta`.

## Areas and Assets

`/v1/areas` is the canonical metadata surface for countries, bidding zones,
control areas, synchronous areas, and market-coupling areas. Country area ids
use ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes.

`/v1/assets` lists physical infrastructure assets with GeoJSON geometry. The
first asset class is GEM operating power plants.

## Time Range

All data endpoints accept `start` and `end` query parameters (ISO 8601 datetime).
Most endpoints default to the last 24 hours. Statistics endpoints default to
dataset-specific historical windows; installed capacity defaults to
`start=2015-01-01` because capacity is slow-moving reference data.

## Sources

Data is collected from 70+ parser modules including ENTSO-E, Energy-Charts (Fraunhofer ISE), Fingrid, SVK (Svenska Kraftnat), Statnett, EIA, BMRS, and many more.

get.description:
List every ``(source, variable)`` pair reachable for ``zone_key``.

For each pair the response includes the source's upstream cadence
(``granularity``), the ENTSO-E document type it is compared against
(``entsoe_baseline``), a free-text note on definitional differences
(``delta_vs_baseline``), the timedatamodel provenance, and a
``default`` flag for the zone's default source per variable.

Sources with no entry in ``config/sources.yaml`` still appear (so
operators can see the zone references them) but with null metadata.

get.description:
Return the dataset's features as a raw GeoJSON FeatureCollection.

The response is a GeoJSON FeatureCollection (not an API envelope), served
with ``Content-Type: application/geo+json`` so it drops straight into
geospatial tooling:

```python
import geopandas as gpd
gdf = gpd.read_file("https://.../v1/geo/world_zones/features")
```

```python
import folium
m = folium.Map()
folium.GeoJson("https://.../v1/geo/entsoe_bzn/features?country=DE").add_to(m)
```

The ``country`` and ``ids`` filters compose (intersection). With neither
filter set, the full FeatureCollection is returned.

get.description:
List all zones with metadata and configured data sources.

Returns every zone visible in the current release environment —
features still staged ``dev`` in ``config/releases.yaml`` are
hidden from the production API. See
:func:`psd.config.reading.load_visible_zones`.

Use this endpoint to discover which zones and sources are available
before querying data endpoints.

Get metadata for a specific zone.

Returns the zone's name, country, timezone, configured data sources,
and preferred source per data type.

The `sources` field shows which data types each source provides
(e.g., `{"entsoe": ["production", "consumption", "price"], "fingrid": ["frequency"]}`).

The `api_source` field shows which source is returned by default
for each data type when no `?source=` parameter is specified.

Example zone keys: `DE`, `SE-SE1`, `NO-NO1`, `FI`, `US-NY-NYIS`.

List every data source available for a zone.

Returns one entry per `(source, variable)` pair configured for the zone,
with granularity, provenance, and a `default` flag indicating which source
is used when no `?source=` parameter is specified.

Example zone keys: `DE`, `SE-SE1`, `FI`.

Discover data availability for a zone as a plottable coverage grid.

Returns bucketed point counts for every time series configured for the
zone. Designed for direct visualisation as a heatmap:

- **y-axis**: each entry in `series` (one per time series)
- **x-axis**: the shared `buckets` array (time)
- **cell value**: `counts[i]` — number of data points in that bucket (0 = missing)

Use `resolution` to control bucket granularity (`1h`, `1d`, `1w`).
Use `source` and/or `provenance` to narrow which series appear.

get.description:
List all configured physical-flow pairs.

Returns every physical-flow pair key in `<zone_from>-><zone_to>`
format (cross-border and inter-zonal — ENTSO-E TR 12.1.G *Physical Flow*).
Use these keys with `GET /v1/exchange/flows/{key}` to query flow data
for a specific pair, or pass a zone key to get all pairs involving
that zone. URL paths keep the legacy `exchange` slug for backwards
compatibility.

Pairs whose endpoints are not visible in the current environment are
omitted (e.g. dev-only zones are excluded from the prod response).

Get metadata for a specific physical-flow pair.

Returns the pair's zone endpoints and configured data sources in
priority order. The first source is the default used by
`GET /v1/exchange/flows/{key}` when no `?source=` is specified.

Example pair keys: `DE->FR`, `SE-SE3->SE-SE4`, `GB->FR`.
Use `GET /v1/exchanges` to list all valid keys.

get.description:
Get electricity production breakdown by production type for a zone.

Returns time series with generation per production type in MW. Each data point
includes all production types that have data for the zone — missing types are
filled with 0.

**Production types**: `solar`, `wind`, `hydro`, `nuclear`, `coal`, `gas`, `oil`,
`biomass`, `geothermal`, `unknown`.

**Multi-source**: Use `?source=` to select a specific data source, or omit
to use the zone's preferred source.

For Swedish bidding zones (SE-SE1 through SE-SE4), the `estimated` source
provides per-zone hydro production estimated from the energy balance
residual, since ENTSO-E only reports aggregated hydro at the national level.

get.description:
Get installed generation capacity for a zone.

The endpoint serves source-specific installed generation capacity in MW:

* `source=entsoe` returns ENTSO-E Transparency Platform article 14.1.A
  document type A68 at annual cadence (`P1Y`).
* `source=ember` returns Ember monthly country-level installed wind and solar
  capacity at monthly cadence (`P1M`) where Ember has coverage.

Use the default `breakdown=fuel` for Rebase fuel rollups such as `wind`,
`solar`, `hydro`, and `nuclear`. Use `breakdown=psr` with `source=entsoe`
when you need raw ENTSO-E PSR columns, for example `B18` for wind offshore
and `B19` for wind onshore. Ember does not expose ENTSO-E PSR columns and
only supports `breakdown=fuel`.

`datetime` and `period_end` describe the upstream validity period.
For ENTSO-E these values should be interpreted as annual stock/reference
values for that period, not as exact measurements taken at `period_end`.
For Ember they mark the monthly capacity period.

Example requests:

```bash
curl -H "X-API-Key: $REBASE_GRID_API_KEY" \
  "https://grid.rebase.energy/api/v1/statistics/installed-capacity/SE?start=2015-01-01T00:00:00Z&end=2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"

curl -H "X-API-Key: $REBASE_GRID_API_KEY" \
  "https://grid.rebase.energy/api/v1/statistics/installed-capacity/SE?breakdown=psr&start=2015-01-01T00:00:00Z&end=2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"

curl -H "X-API-Key: $REBASE_GRID_API_KEY" \
  "https://grid.rebase.energy/api/v1/statistics/installed-capacity/DE?source=ember&start=2024-01-01T00:00:00Z&end=2024-04-01T00:00:00Z"
```

get.description:
Get total system load (consumption) for a zone.

Returns time series of total electricity consumption in MW.

**Multi-source**: Use `?source=` to select a specific data source, or omit
to use the area's preferred source. Use `GET /v1/areas/{area_id}` to see
available sources.

The virtual source `energy_balance` composes load from production, storage
discharge, and net exchange flows. Prefer it for zones with pumped
storage (DE, CH, AT, PT, ...) where the ENTSO-E raw A65 value
over-reports.

**Response fields**:
- `load_mw`: Total system load in megawatts.
- `source`: The data source used for this response.

parameters.name: source

schema.description: Data source to query. Options include real upstream sources (e.g. `entsoe`, `energy_charts`) plus the virtual source `energy_balance`, which computes load from ``production + storage_discharge − net_exports``. Omit to use the zone's preferred source.
schema.title: Source

parameters.description: Data source to query. Options include real upstream sources (e.g. `entsoe`, `energy_charts`) plus the virtual source `energy_balance`, which computes load from ``production + storage_discharge − net_exports``. Omit to use the zone's preferred source.

parameters.name: variant

schema.description: Endpoint variant for sources that publish multiple semantically distinct series. Example: `?source=bmrs&variant=itsdo` returns Elexon's transmission-boundary demand (ITSDO); omitting the parameter selects the source's configured `default_variant` from `config/sources.yaml` (`b0610` for `bmrs` = A65). Sources without a variants block ignore this parameter.

get.description:
Get measured physical electricity flows (ENTSO-E TR 12.1.G).

Returns **measured physical flow** — not commercial or nominated schedules
(TR 12.1.F). Covers both cross-border and inter-zonal pairs (e.g. IT-NO↔IT-CNO,
IT-CAL↔IT-SIC). URL keeps the legacy `exchange` slug for backwards compatibility.

`key` can be either a **zone key** or a **flow pair key**:

- **Zone key** (e.g. `DE`): returns all pairs involving that zone
  (`DE->FR`, `DE->NL`, `DE->AT`, …).
- **Flow pair key** (e.g. `DE->FR`): returns data for that single
  pair only. Use `GET /v1/exchanges` to list all valid pair keys.

**Response fields**:
- `net_flow`: Physical flow in MW. For zone queries, oriented to the
  queried zone — positive means the queried zone is *exporting*.
  For pair queries, oriented to the `zone_from` in the pair key —
  positive means flow from `zone_from` to `zone_to`.

get.description:
Get cross-border transfer capacity (NTC / MaxBex) for a zone pair.

Returns the **TSO-allocated commercial transfer capacity** — the maximum
MW market participants can schedule. This is forward-looking and reflects
reliability margins (TRM), N-1 security, and flow-based allocation; it is
typically a fraction of the physical line nameplate rating. **Not** the
same as PyPSA `s_nom` line capacity (also surfaced in the map UI), which
is the engineering thermal nameplate.

**Capacity is asymmetric**: the MW available from A→B is not the same
as B→A. This endpoint returns both directions for the requested pair
in a single response under ``series``:

- ``direction = "forward"`` — capacity in the requested A→B direction.
- ``direction = "reverse"`` — capacity in the opposite B→A direction.

Values are always non-negative MW (direction is encoded in
``direction``, not in the sign of the number).

**Sources**:

- ``entsoe`` (A61 NTC forecasts; default) — Net Transfer Capacity, covers
  most non-flow-based borders.
- ``jao`` (MaxBex) — Maximum Bilateral Exchange for flow-based regions
  (CORE, Nordic, SWE, Italy-North, Cross-CCR) where A61 returns nothing.

Requests with ``from_zone`` and ``to_zone`` swapped relative to the
canonical edge in ``exchanges.yaml`` are accepted — the response
flips the forward/reverse mapping accordingly. ``canonical_edge`` in
the response always echoes the underlying catalog key so callers can
re-key against their own state if needed.

ProductionColumnData.title: ProductionColumnData
ProductionColumnData.description:
Column-form production data in MW.

``datetime`` is always present; additional fields are per-mode
arrays (``solar``, ``wind``, ``hydro``, ``nuclear``, ``coal``,
``gas``, ``oil``, ``biomass``, ``geothermal``, ``unknown``). Only
modes with at least one non-null observation in the window appear
as columns. Within a column, timestamps where the mode had no
reported value carry ``null`` — when ``resolution=native`` (the
default) values are *never* forward-filled across modes that
publish at different cadences; the response shows the raw publish
grid honestly. When the caller passes ``resolution=15M`` (or any
explicit grid), each mode is mean-downsampled or ffill-upsampled
onto that grid before the column is emitted (carry-forward is
capped at one upstream publication interval).
All columns are the same length as ``datetime``.

native_resolution.description: Per-mode upstream cadence as an ISO-8601 duration (e.g. `PT60M`, `PT15M`). `null` when the cadence couldn't be inferred from the window (typically: too few samples). Useful for comparing modes published at different rates within the same zone.

derivation.description: For DERIVED and RECONSTRUCTION categories: a short formula or rule string, e.g. ``production + storage_discharge − net_exports``.

upstream_sources.title: Upstream Sources
upstream_sources.description: For DERIVED and RECONSTRUCTION categories: list of source short names whose observations this value was composed from.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description:
Annotation describing what kind of data a response carries.

``category`` is the leaf from the spec. ``kind`` is derived from
``category`` via :data:`KIND_BY_CATEGORY` — if a caller sets only
``category``, the validator fills in ``kind``; if both are set, they
must agree (otherwise we silently let the caller lie about whether
their data is ACTUAL or CALCULATED).

The remaining fields are optional evidence that's only meaningful
for some categories:

* ``description`` — one-line human-readable explanation of how the
  data was produced (e.g. upstream document type, model method).
* ``issue_time`` — for FORECAST/PREDICTION only. Omitted elsewhere.
* ``derivation`` + ``upstream_sources`` — for DERIVED and
  RECONSTRUCTION, a formula string plus the list of upstream source
  short names whose observations fed the computation.

Column-form storage data in MW.

Same schema as :class:`ProductionColumnData` except the extra

tags.name: Geo

Filter with `?country=` or `?ids=`, or pin a specific version with `?version=YYYY-MM-DD`. Available datasets: `world_zones`, `entsoe_cty`, `entsoe_bzn`, `entsoe_cta`.

tags.name: Areas
tags.description: Canonical metadata for countries, bidding zones, TSO/control areas, synchronous areas, and market-coupling areas. Country area ids use ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes; legacy zone keys remain valid identifiers for bidding/control areas.

tags.name: Assets
tags.description: Physical infrastructure assets with GeoJSON geometry. Current data covers GEM operating power plants; the schema can also represent future line assets.

tags.name: Zones
tags.description: Zone metadata — list zones, see which data types are available, and discover data sources per zone.

tags.name: Physical flow pairs
tags.description: Lists all configured cross-border and inter-zonal physical flow pairs (ENTSO-E TR 12.1.G *Physical Flow*). Use a pair key with `GET /v1/exchange/flows/{key}` to query the flow data. URL paths keep the legacy `exchange` slug for backwards compatibility.

tags.name: Production
tags.description: Electricity generation broken down by fuel type (solar, wind, hydro, nuclear, coal, gas, oil, biomass, geothermal). Values in MW.

tags.name: Statistics
tags.description: Period aggregate and reference datasets. Installed capacity is available from ENTSO-E annual A68 and Ember monthly capacity; Ember also provides country-level monthly and annual electricity generation, demand, power-sector emissions, and carbon intensity.

tags.name: Consumption
tags.description: Total electricity consumption (system load). Values in MW.

tags.name: Storage
tags.description: Net storage output — pumped hydro and battery discharge. Positive values mean discharging to the grid. Values in MW.

tags.name: Physical flow
tags.description: Measured cross-border (and inter-zonal) physical electricity flows — ENTSO-E TR 12.1.G *Physical Flow*. **Not** commercial / nominated schedules (TR 12.1.F). Values in MW. URL paths keep the legacy `exchange` slug for backwards compatibility.

tags.name: Transfer capacity
tags.description: Cross-border transfer capacity (NTC and MaxBex) per direction. Sources: ENTSO-E A61 Net Transfer Capacity forecasts for NTC borders, JAO MaxBex for flow-based regions (CORE, Nordic, SWE, Italy-North, Cross-CCR). Capacity is asymmetric — both directions are returned in a single call. Values in MW.

tags.name: Prices
tags.description: Day-ahead spot market electricity prices. Values in EUR/MWh (USD/MWh for US zones).

tags.name: Frequency
tags.description: Grid frequency in Hz. Frequency is measured per synchronous area, not per zone — the Nordic grid, for example, has one shared frequency. Query by zone or by synchronous area code (NSA, CESA, GBSA, ISA, BSA, IPSA).
